_note: Curated sense lists for terms that carry more than one meaning. Keys must match a term in data/lingo.json exactly. Senses are drawn from the sources the entry already cites (Green's, the OED, the LSA material, the Wikipedia articles, Smitherman/Major/Rickford) — this file adds structure, not new claims. scripts/attach_examples.py merges these into the reference.

cuff / cuffing season.label: the season
cuff / cuffing season.gloss: The cold months, when pairing up is treated as a timed collective project.

cuff / cuffing season.label: the act
cuff / cuffing season.gloss: To cuff someone: to secure a partner before the window closes. Implies acquisition, with a hint of reluctance.

cuff / cuffing season.label: the joke the title makes
cuff / cuffing season.gloss: The 2026 episode title rewrites the original's 'those who can't teach, tutor' as 'those who can't commit, cuff' — the same sentence shape, a different failure.

throwing shade.label: literal
throwing shade.gloss: Shadow — the OED sense, still the primary one outside the idiom.

throwing shade.label: the idiom
throwing shade.gloss: Indirect disparagement: the target must work out that they were insulted. Distinguished from a direct insult precisely by the deniability.

throwing shade.label: as a verb
throwing shade.gloss: 'To shade someone' — to deliver it. Grammatically transitive, which is what makes it a practice rather than just a noun.

reading (someone).label: the insult sense
reading (someone).gloss: To name a person's faults in public, with accuracy as the criterion — a bad read fails and is forgotten.

reading (someone).label: the skill sense
reading (someone).gloss: 'She can read' — an acknowledged competence, judged by wit and precision, not by kindness.

reading (someone).label: the ordinary sense
reading (someone).gloss: Reading text. The course lives on this ambiguity: a text that 'reads' its characters is doing the first thing, on purpose.

signifying / signifyin'.label: the speech practice
signifying / signifyin'.gloss: Indirect, artful verbal critique — boasting, insult, commentary and warning carried by implication.

signifying / signifyin'.label: the literary theory sense
signifying / signifyin'.gloss: Signifyin(g) as a theory of Black literary practice: repetition with a difference, revision as creation. The spelling with the bracketed (g) marks this second life.

bougie / bourgie.label: adjective
bougie / bourgie.gloss: Aspirational, status-conscious, inclined to class policing — 'that's so bougie'.

bougie / bourgie.label: noun
bougie / bourgie.gloss: A person who behaves that way. Used inside the group, and always an argument about class as much as about taste.

bougie / bourgie.label: as a class critique
bougie / bourgie.gloss: In the show's world it marks the gap between students who work and students whose families own the dormitory.

the dozens.label: the game
the dozens.gloss: Competitive insult exchange, traditionally trading on family, judged by wit and audience reaction.

the dozens.label: the variant
the dozens.gloss: The 'dirty dozens' — the escalated form, which is why the tradition is often described with a warning attached.

the dozens.label: the origin story
the dozens.gloss: The 1991 episode explicitly takes up where the practice comes from, which is our only documented case of the show framing a verbal tradition as history.

line.label: Greek life
line.gloss: A pledge class, or the group that crosses together — 'her line'.

line.label: performance
line.gloss: The formation in stepping: the line is both the group and its shape.

line.label: romance
line.gloss: 'A line' as the opening move — the pick-up line, which is the individual-scale version of the same competitive wit.

hook up.label: connection
hook up.gloss: To meet or be introduced — 'we hooked up through a friend'.

hook up.label: intimacy
hook up.gloss: A casual sexual or romantic encounter; the 1980s-90s usage the original's summary records.

hook up.label: technical
hook up.gloss: To connect equipment. Included because the collision of senses is why the term is so often deliberately vague.

the Pit.label: the place
the Pit.gloss: Hillman's campus food spot and hangout, run by Mr. Gaines — where students work and where the money plots live.

the Pit.label: the pun
the Pit.gloss: A pit is also a hole and an orchestra pit. The name of the least glamorous place on a status-obsessed campus is doing quiet work.

probate.label: Greek life
probate.gloss: A chapter's public presentation of its new members — performance as announcement.

probate.label: the legal sense
probate.gloss: The court process for settling an estate. The collision is instructive: both senses are about transferring standing in public.

stepping.label: the movement
stepping.gloss: An ordinary step. The point is that the dance takes its name from the plainest possible verb.

stepping.label: the tradition
stepping.gloss: Stepping: rhythmic, percussive group dance in formation, with Greek-letter, dorm and team variants.

stepping.label: the event
stepping.gloss: A step show — competitive, judged, and often the centre of a homecoming weekend.

tea.label: the drink
tea.gloss: Tea. In the original's world it also names a formal social event — the annual freshman tea a dean hosts.

tea.label: the gossip
tea.gloss: 'The tea' as the news worth having, and 'spill the tea' as the request to hand it over.

periodt.label: the punctuation
periodt.gloss: A full stop — the ordinary mark that ends a sentence.

periodt.label: the verdict
periodt.gloss: In AAVE-derived usage, 'period' ends the discussion; 'periodt' intensifies it. The claim is closed and further argument is refused.

sus.label: the clipping
sus.gloss: Suspicious, or a suspicious person — modern clipping of 'suspect'.

sus.label: the older verb
sus.gloss: To suss (something) out: to work it out by investigation. Recorded in British and American usage long before the clipping.

mess.label: affectionate accusation
mess.gloss: 'You are a mess' — chaotic, and loved for it. The term of endearment that runs through the original's domestic register.

mess.label: the situation
mess.gloss: 'Same mess, different clock speed' — the way this project describes a social problem recurring across 39 years.

drag.label: performance
drag.gloss: Drag: the performance tradition of exaggerated gendered presentation, and the culture from which the vocabulary of reading and shade was popularised well beyond it.

call and response.label: the institution
call and response.gloss: Church — in Black American life a central institution of community, politics and music, and the origin of much of the register both series rely on.

call and response.label: the affirmation
call and response.gloss: 'Church!' as agreement: the congregation's role crossing from the sanctuary into general speech.

call and response.label: the classroom
call and response.gloss: A student completing the professor's line, or a room answering a performer. It is the same move in every setting, and it is why a Black classroom can sound like a call and a response at once.

homecoming.label: the weekend
homecoming.gloss: The annual return of alumni: game, band, step show, reunions, and a campus that briefly belongs to its former students.

homecoming.label: the ritual function
homecoming.gloss: What Durkheim would call a collective effervescence event: the group generates the feeling, then treats it as proof of the group's reality.

homecoming.label: the money
homecoming.gloss: Homecoming is also a fundraising apparatus — a fact the 2026 season's budget plot makes impossible to ignore.
